_comment: Ground truth for lexical (BM25) retrieval over the Treasure Island fixture.
PRECISION (always applied) — `must_contain` is a substring that EVERY
returned passage must contain, case-insensitively. This is the assertion
that the lexical arm is doing exact matching rather than returning
plausible-looking noise, and it holds for every term regardless of how
RECALL (only where honest) — `expect_chapters` lists chapters of which at
least one must appear within `recall_limit` hits. This is deliberately
restricted to terms whose occurrences really are concentrated in a known
stretch of the book. For a name like Flint or Hispaniola that recurs
throughout, BM25's top hits are whichever passages have the highest term
density, which is NOT a property worth asserting -- so those queries carry
an empty `expect_chapters` and are checked for precision only. Asserting a
chapter there would be testing term-density accidents, not retrieval.
Chapter numbers are the sequential 1..34 indices emitted by the fixture

queries.name: rare_boat_word
queries.note: Ben Gunn's homemade boat. A rare word confined to Jim's sea adventure -- the strongest precision+recall signal in the book.

queries.name: marooned_character
queries.note: Ben Gunn is introduced in 'The Man of the Island' (15) and recurs to the end.

queries.name: inn_name
queries.note: The Admiral Benbow inn dominates Part One.

queries.name: ship_name
queries.note: The schooner. Recurs from Part Two to the end -- precision only, no honest chapter expectation.

queries.name: doctor
queries.note: Named in the opening paragraph but present throughout -- precision only.

queries.name: captain
queries.note: Present from Part Two onward -- precision only.

queries.name: dead_pirate
queries.note: Invoked constantly by the crew across the whole novel -- precision only.

must_return_nothing.note: Modern scientific term; cannot occur in a 19th-century sea novel.
Anachronism guard -- proves we are not returning arbitrary filler.
